title: Global cohomological bounds from perfect models
statement: Let X be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], A a commutative Noetherian adically complete ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring] with unique maximal ideal I, and let K satisfy IsSfbStratifiedPerfect [def-sfb-adic-stratified-perfect-data]. Then K has an ordered integral cohomological vanishing interval, and the derived residue Q.obj(sfbResidueComplex X I K) has an ordered integral cohomological vanishing interval.

lean.statement:
theorem adicPerfectModels_cohomologicalBounds (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X]
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.IsMaximal ∧ ∀ J : Ideal A, J.IsMaximal → J = I)
    [IsAdicComplete I A]
    (K : DerivedCategory (proEtaleRingModules X (adicLisseCompletedRing X I)))
    (hK : IsSfbStratifiedPerfect X I K) :
    (∃ a b : ℤ, a ≤ b ∧ ∀ q : ℤ, q < a ∨ b < q →
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ q).obj K)) ∧
    (∃ a b : ℤ, a ≤ b ∧ ∀ q : ℤ, q < a ∨ b < q →
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ q).obj
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (sfbResidueComplex X I K))))

proof.text: On each Noetherian stratum use the finite-cover extraction in ProEtaleTorLocalGlobal. The family of all selected charts is finite. If their model intervals are [a_j,b_j], the interval [-sum_j |a_j|,sum_j |b_j|] is ordered and contains every interval; for an empty family it is [0,0].

source.place: Lemma 6.5.3 and Proposition 6.6.11, reverse implication: local bounded models and finite-stratum globalization

proof.text: A term of a model outside its interval is zero. Additive constant realization and completed scalar extension preserve zero objects, hence the completed model has zero cohomology there. Exact module inverse image and slice restriction, their derived localization comparisons, and the given local model isomorphism transport this vanishing to the restriction of H^q(K). Identity scalar extension is identified with module inverse image by uniqueness of its adjunction.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.3 and Proposition 6.6.11, reverse implication: local bounded models and finite-stratum globalization

proof.text: Slice-cover separation gives zero inverse image on each stratum. Apply the jointly surjective immersion detection lemma abDetectMaps to the underlying additive sheaf, using the module inverse-image comparison. Faithfulness of the forgetful functor then gives H^q(K)=0 globally.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.3 and Proposition 6.6.11, reverse implication: local bounded models and finite-stratum globalization

proof.text: On the same finite set of charts apply the single-chart local residue bound with the selected perfect model and its specified interval. The common interval lies outside each local interval whenever it lies outside the sum interval. Sheaf separation on slice covers and abDetectMaps on the strata give zero underlying additive sheaf for residue cohomology; the faithful forgetful functor reflects zero. Pair this global residue bound with the bound already established for K.
